calls.reason: Bain's 2025 report gives a similar figure of about $2T in yearly revenue by 2030. But that is a scenario for the whole industry under scaling assumptions, not a requirement modelled for hyperscalers. And 'make sense' is a judgement call.

This is a conditional forecast whose condition has not happened. The packet shows no move to full-cost pricing. Anthropic's S-1 losses and adjusted figures say nothing about how demand would respond to sustainable prices.

Menlo's $37B enterprise estimate covers a narrower market and cannot check the $65B total. No cost or demand evidence tests whether all demand depends on subsidies or would vanish at full-cost prices.

Anthropic's announcement confirms the $30B round on February 12, 2026. But the investor statements credit revenue growth and enterprise adoption, and nothing in the packet links the round to a publicity campaign.

S&P moved its outlook to negative, credit default swaps widened, and the bridge loan matures in March 2027, all of which point to real strain. But the LTV breach was only a projection and only $10B of the facility was drawn, so 'very precarious' is not clearly established.
Cursor's pricing change shows token costs feeding into what customers pay, but there is no churn data. Lindy reports cutting costs while keeping retention. Nothing links the three steps in the chain.
